title: The Gospel of Luke
iconGap: the shared pool and Luke's own Feast-cycle harvest (2026-09-25c) have both been searched against all 152 passages; what is left was not found in the Orthodox programmes this project has enumerated — some of it (a few of Luke's parables and miracles, some Passion moments) may simply not exist as a distinct Orthodox icon, and some may be findable in a source not yet searched (see HANDOFF Next for what was tried). Christ at twelve years has its own note: the one candidate found is catalogued as a Mid-Pentecost icon, and whether the resemblance is enough to use it anyway is the owner's open question — see HANDOFF Gotchas and Next
catenaShort: Quoted from the Catena Aurea on the Gospel of St Luke, compiled by St Thomas Aquinas from the Fathers, in the Oxford translation of 1843 (public domain) as given in the Dominican House of Studies electronic edition, which modernises the second-person pronouns and omits the marginal references to each Father’s work.
catenaLong: The patristic commentary is quoted from the Catena Aurea on St Luke — the “golden chain” of the Fathers compiled by St Thomas Aquinas — in the Oxford translation of 1843 (public domain), as given in the Dominican House of Studies electronic edition, which modernises the second-person pronouns and omits the marginal references to each Father’s work; nothing is paraphrased. It is restricted here to Fathers venerated in the Orthodox Church, and to Blessed Theophylact of Ohrid, whose commentary on the Gospels is the standard Orthodox reading of them. This volume leans on St Cyril of Alexandria, whose commentary on St Luke survives largely in the Syriac, and on St Ambrose, who wrote the great Latin exposition of this Gospel; the Carolingians, the medieval Glossa, Origen and Eusebius are excluded here as they are in the other readers.
